implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2023) was revised and approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). Account management and access review procedures under STD-06 are being written (due 2026-12-31).

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); LMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Staff and faculty accounts are created in the identity provider from the ERP HR feed and federated to the SIS, LMS, FAMS, CRM, and cloud. Student accounts are created when the SIS marks an applicant admitted. Gaps: access reviews are annual (last February 2026), not semiannual; about 140 local LMS accounts (clinical preceptors, guest instructors, contractors) sit outside the identity provider and are not reviewed (P07 found 19 inactive for more than 180 days); the third-party servicer creates its own FAMS accounts.
evidence: HR feed configuration; IdP and LMS user exports; access review record February 2026

implementation_statement: Account creation, disablement, and removal for staff, faculty, and students run through the identity provider's automated workflow driven by the ERP and SIS.
Staff accounts inactive for 90 days are disabled automatically. Gap: local LMS accounts and FAMS servicer accounts are not covered.

provider_if_inherited: SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FAMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2, Security only); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: The SIS, FAMS, LMS, and cloud enforce the role-based access the college defines (64 SIS roles). Role design issues are tracked under AC-6.
evidence: SIS role catalog; FAMS roles; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: Cloud hub firewall rules control flows between the workloads, shared services, and campus networks. Gap: Campus 3 has no internal segmentation, so lab and campus safety traffic reaches staff systems.
evidence: Hub firewall rule export; Campus 3 network diagram

implementation_statement: Financial aid staff award aid in the FAMS; only student accounts staff post disbursements and release refunds in the SIS. No user holds both roles (34 CFR 668.16(c)(2)). Quarterly role conflict report reviewed by the Chief Compliance Officer.
evidence: SIS and FAMS role conflict report Q2 2026

implementation_statement: Roles are least-privilege by design. Gaps: admissions and all 45 advisors can see full SIS student records including financial aid holds; 46 data warehouse users can query all student-level data, including ISIR-derived fields; privileged access management covers the cloud only.
evidence: SIS role matrix; data warehouse grants export

implementation_statement: Cloud administrators use separate privileged identities through the cloud privileged access broker. Gap: 9 IT staff use their everyday accounts for identity provider, SIS, and LMS administration.

Privileged roles are limited to named IT staff in the cloud (11 identities). Gap: SaaS administrator roles (identity provider 7, SIS 6, LMS 9, FAMS 4) have standing access and are reviewed only annually.
evidence: Admin role exports from each system

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks an account for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts and applies smart lockout against password spraying for all SSO applications.
Staff endpoints lock after 10 minutes of inactivity through device management; lab computers log off after 15 minutes idle.

provider_if_inherited: SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FAMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2, Security only)
implementation_statement: SIS and FAMS sessions end after 30 minutes idle for staff and 20 minutes for the student portal.

Staff remote access uses SaaS over TLS with SSO and MFA; administrative access to cloud workloads uses the privileged access broker. Gap: the third-party servicer reaches the FAMS with local accounts without MFA.
evidence: VPN and broker configuration; FAMS servicer account list

implementation_statement: Staff Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication with device certificates; student and guest Wi-Fi is isolated from staff networks at Campuses 1 and 2. Campus 3 Wi-Fi is isolated, but its wired network is flat (AC-4).
College-owned mobile devices are enrolled in device management. Gap: faculty may use personal phones for email without app protection policies.
POL-05 limits use of personal computers to SaaS through the browser. Gap: no technical control stops downloads of SIS reports to personal computers.

Disclosures from education records follow FERPA consent and exceptions; employer partners receive progress data only with written student consent. Gap: disclosure records (99.32) are kept in the SIS for transcript requests but not for data sent through the integration platform to vendors.
evidence: FERPA consent forms; SIS disclosure log

implementation_statement: Training requirements are in POL-05 (approved 2026-09-17). A training procedure with role-based curricula is due 2026-12-31.
Annual FERPA, Safeguards Rule, and security awareness training for all employees, with quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 9.4%). Completion 94% for fiscal 2026.
The annual course covers misuse of student data by insiders. Gap: no content on recognizing refund fraud by staff or servicer personnel.
Phishing simulations and a module on social engineering, including help-desk impersonation used to reset student accounts, run each quarter.
Security staff receive annual technical training and the MSSP briefs them monthly. Gap: no role-based training for financial aid, student accounts, service desk, or system administrators.
Logging requirements are stated in POL-03; the logging and monitoring standard STD-02 is in draft (due 2027-01-31).

Identity provider, email, firewall, cloud control-plane, and EDR events go to the SIEM. Gap: SIS, FAMS, and LMS audit events (record views, grade changes, refund bank changes, exports) are not collected.

provider_if_inherited: SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FAMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2, Security only)
implementation_statement: Collected records include user, time, source, action, and object. SIS and FAMS audit records include the same fields but stay in the applications.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews SIEM alerts 24x7. Gap: no routine review of user activity in the SIS or FAMS; the 23 portal takeovers in 2025-26 were found by students, not by monitoring.
Cloud logs land in a write-once log bucket in the shared services account; SIEM records are protected by the MSSP platform.
The SIEM keeps 12 months searchable; cloud logs are kept 3 years in the log bucket. Gap: SIS and FAMS logs are kept only for the vendor default of 180 days.

provider_if_inherited: SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FAMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2, Security only); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Audit generation is enabled on all cloud accounts and SaaS systems. Gap: the data warehouse does not log queries by user.
evidence: Cloud trail configuration; data warehouse settings

implementation_statement: Assessment and continuous monitoring responsibilities are in POL-01 (approved 2026-09-17). An assessment procedure is due 2026-12-31.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses selected controls each year (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21). The independent Title IV compliance audit also tests Safeguards Rule elements.

Interconnections with the Department of Education (SAIG), the bank, and the third-party servicer are governed by agreements. Gap: no written interconnection terms for 6 of the 37 integration platform interfaces (payment plan vendor, emergency notification service, and 4 employer partner file feeds).
The POA&M (P07) is kept by the GRC analyst and reported quarterly to the audit committee.
The CIO accepted operation of the SILP with conditions on 2026-09-17 (P02 section 4.2); High risks were accepted by the President and CEO.

Continuous monitoring covers EDR, the SIEM, cloud posture management, and quarterly vulnerability scans. Gap: SaaS application logs are not monitored (AU-2), so monitoring is not continuous for the SIS and FAMS, and 314.4(d)(2) testing therefore still relies on annual penetration testing and semiannual vulnerability assessments.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: An external penetration test was performed in November 2025. Gap: it covered internet-facing systems only; no internal or student portal test, and the scope was not set from the risk assessment as 314.4(d)(2)(i) requires.
Configuration management policy statements are in POL-01; the configuration standard STD-01 is in draft (due 2027-03-31).
Gold images exist for staff endpoints and lab computers. Gap: no documented baselines for cloud virtual machines, the integration platform, or SaaS tenant settings.

Changes to cloud infrastructure go through tickets with approval. Gap: SIS configuration changes and integration platform job changes are made without tickets or a second reviewer (P07 found 9 of 20 sampled changes undocumented).
evidence: Change tickets; integration platform job history

implementation_statement: Impact analysis is done informally for major SaaS releases. Gap: no security impact analysis for integration changes that move student data.
Organization guardrails deny public storage and unencrypted volumes. Gap: no benchmark-based hardening for virtual machines; 3 of 10 sampled servers failed more than 20% of benchmark checks.
Unneeded services are disabled on the gold images. Gap: SaaS AI features are enabled by default in new releases without review (P10).

Asset inventory from device management, the cloud, and the SaaS register. Gap: campus safety devices and Campus 3 network gear are not in the inventory; the SaaS register misses 14 department-purchased tools.
Staff cannot install software without IT approval (device management allow-list). Lab computers reset to the image at reboot.
Contingency statements are in POL-03 and POL-04; the contingency and recovery standard STD-07 is due 2026-12-31.
Gap: no IT disaster recovery plan. The BIA (P05) now sets RTOs and RPOs; the plan is due 2026-12-31 and must include the emergency notification break-glass path (34 CFR 668.46(g)).
Gap: no contingency training. Training for recovery roles follows the plan (due 2027-02-28).
Gap: no restore test of the integration platform, data warehouse, or employer partner portal has ever been run. Quarterly restore tests start 2026-10-27 with the integration platform.
Backups are stored in the backup account in a second region with separate credentials.
Workloads can be rebuilt in the second region from images and backups. Gap: the rebuild has not been documented or tested.
Campus 1 has dual internet with cellular failover. Gap: Campuses 2 and 3 have one carrier each.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2); SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); LMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Daily backups of the workloads account to the write-once backup vault (30 days); SaaS vendors back up their platforms. P07 confirmed 30 of 30 July backup jobs succeeded.
Gap: recovery and reconstitution procedures do not exist for college-managed workloads (due with the IT DR plan 2026-12-31).
Identification and authentication statements are in POL-02; the authenticator standard STD-06 needs an update (due 2026-12-31).

Staff, faculty, and students have unique identities in the identity provider. Gap: 140 local LMS accounts and the servicer's 8 FAMS accounts are outside the identity provider; IT students share a lab admin account in the Campus 3 cybersecurity lab.
evidence: IdP export; LMS and FAMS local accounts

implementation_statement: MFA is enforced for all privileged accounts in the identity provider and the cloud.

MFA is enforced for all staff and faculty. Gap: students may opt out (54% enrolled), and the servicer's FAMS accounts have no MFA; no written Qualified Individual approval of equivalent controls exists for either.
Push MFA with number matching is replay resistant for staff. Gap: students who opted in may use SMS codes.
Identifiers are assigned from the HR and SIS records and never reused.

Passwords: 14 characters minimum with a banned list for staff; 10 for students. Gaps: 410 lab computers at Campuses 2 and 3 share one local administrator password; 6 integration service account passwords have not been rotated since 2023.
evidence: IdP password policy; local admin audit

provider_if_inherited: SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FAMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2, Security only)
implementation_statement: Non-organizational users (students, applicants, servicer staff, employer partner users, preceptors) authenticate to the student portal, aid portal, partner portal, or LMS. Gap: partner portal users have password-only sign-in.

Gap: changing refund bank details in the student portal does not require re-authentication or out-of-band confirmation. Step-up MFA plus a confirmation call or email to the prior contact is due 2026-11-30.
Online applicants are identity-proofed by admissions staff before aid packaging. Gap: checks are manual and inconsistent; 41 likely fraudulent applicants reached enrollment in fall 2025.
evidence: Admissions identity check procedure; fraud log

implementation_statement: Applicants submit a government ID for online programs. Gap: evidence requirements differ by admissions team.
Gap: ID documents are viewed, not validated. A document and liveness verification service for online applicants is planned for the January 2027 start.
POL-03 was approved 2026-09-17 and now addresses the 314.4(h) elements; supporting procedures are the P08 runbooks.
Security staff and the MSSP are trained in incident handling. Gap: executives, financial aid, and student accounts staff have not trained on the new runbooks.
Gap: the last tabletop was in 2024. An executive ransomware tabletop is set for 2026-11-10 and a fraud tabletop for 2027-01-20.
The MSSP contains endpoint threats 24x7 and escalates within 30 minutes. Gap: 2025-26 refund fraud cases were handled by the Bursar without security involvement or root-cause analysis.
Incidents are tracked in the IT service management tool with a security category and discovery time field (added 2026-08).
Staff report incidents to the service desk security line. Gap: no procedure existed for the FTC notice (314.4(j)), the FSA breach notice, or OIG fraud referrals until P08 (approved 2026-09-17).
Incident response assistance is available from the MSSP and from the cyber insurer's panel forensic firm.
The P08 runbooks and POL-03 form the incident response plan. Gap: not yet exercised (IR-3).
Maintenance of campus network equipment follows vendor schedules and change tickets.
Vendor remote support for cloud workloads uses the privileged access broker. Gap: the access control vendor reaches Campus 3 door controllers through its own always-on remote tool.
evidence: Broker logs; vendor remote access list

implementation_statement: Media handling is in POL-04 (approved 2026-09-17).
Retired staff drives are wiped and certified by a disposal vendor. Gap: copier and multifunction printer drives returned at lease end have no sanitization certificate (4 of 4 returns in 2025-26).
Physical security statements are in POL-01. Facility standard STD-10 exists from 2023 and needs a Campus 3 update.
Badge access to administrative offices and network closets is approved by department heads and campus safety.
Badge readers control administrative offices and network closets at Campuses 1 and 2; cloud and SaaS data centers are inherited. Gap: Campus 3 network closets use keys without a key log.
Planning policy is in POL-01; SSP maintenance procedure due 2026-12-31.
This SSP (version 1.0, 2026-09-17) documents the SILP and its controls.
Employees acknowledge POL-05 at hire and annually (acknowledgment rate 96%). Students accept the acceptable use terms at first portal sign-in.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The WISP (2023, updated 2025) and POL-01 form the program plan. Gap: the program plan does not yet include the AI governance process or the standards issue schedule.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The vCISO is the Qualified Individual, designated in writing in January 2025; the CIO is the senior member who directs and oversees the Qualified Individual; the consulting contract requires the firm to maintain its own security program (314.4(a)(1)-(3)).
evidence: Designation memo 2025-01; consulting contract security schedule

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Risk management strategy with acceptance authorities and appetite statements approved 2026-09-17 (P01). The Qualified Individual reports in writing to the board at least annually.
Personnel security statements are in POL-01 and POL-02.
Background checks for all employees with access to student financial records, run at hire.

Terminations disable identity provider access automatically on the termination date. Gap: adjunct faculty between terms keep access because contracts end without an ERP termination (P07 found 5 of 25 sampled departures active more than 30 days).
Transfers trigger a role change ticket. Gap: prior SIS roles are not removed (P07 found 6 of 25 sampled transfers kept old roles).
Contracts for the servicer, MSSP, and vCISO firm include confidentiality terms. Gap: 22 vendors with student data lack FERPA school-official and security terms.
Sanctions for policy violations are in POL-01 and the employee handbook; 3 sanctions recorded in fiscal 2026.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Gap: ISIR-derived fields are copied to the data warehouse and used for the AI-002 model and enrollment marketing analytics. The HEA limits FAFSA data to the application, award, and administration of aid. Fields are to be removed by 2026-11-30.
regulatory_driver: HEA sec. 483 (FSA Handbook Vol. 2 Ch. 7); N61-R02 (314.4(c)(2))

implementation_statement: Risk assessment policy is in POL-01 (annual risk assessment and after material changes).
The SILP is categorized Moderate under FIPS 199 (section 6 of this SSP).
Written risk assessment using NIST SP 800-30, completed 2026-07-31 (P01, 52 risks), meeting the 314.4(b)(1) content requirements.
Supply chain risk is assessed at onboarding. Gap: no tiering or periodic reassessment (P09 tiering adopted 2026-09-17).

Quarterly authenticated scans of cloud and campus systems; monthly external scans. Gap: Critical findings exceed the 30-day target (P07: 12 of 40 sampled findings late); lab and campus safety networks are not scanned.
Each risk has a treatment, owner, and due date in P01; acceptances follow POL-01 4.4.
Purchasing requires a security review for systems holding student data. Gap: 14 SaaS tools (including AI-003 and AI-004) were bought by departments on cards without review.
External services are governed by contracts. Gaps: 22 vendors lack FERPA school-official and security terms; 31 contracts lack incident notice terms; SOC 2 reports reviewed only at onboarding.
Unsupported components are tracked for staff systems. Gap: 64 door controllers and 11 video recorders run unsupported firmware; replacement is in the 2027 capital plan.

Cloud hub firewall and campus firewalls protect the boundary; workloads have no internet ingress except the partner portal through a web application firewall. Gap: Campus 3 flat network and an unisolated cybersecurity lab.

control_name: Deny by Default: Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default rules apply in the cloud hub. Gap: campus firewalls at Campus 3 allow any-to-any internally.

provider_if_inherited: SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); LMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); FAMS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2, Security only)
implementation_statement: TLS 1.2 or higher protects SaaS, portal, and interface traffic. Gap: financial aid staff email ISIR and award spreadsheets to the servicer without encryption (P07 found 7 of 20 sampled messages unencrypted).
Keys for cloud workloads and backups are managed in the cloud key service, with separate backup keys and annual rotation.
Encryption uses FIPS-validated modules in the cloud and SaaS services.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2); SIS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Encryption at rest is on for all cloud storage, SaaS systems, and staff endpoints. Gap: spreadsheets with ISIR data on the file service are encrypted by the platform but shared broadly (AC-6).
Patches are deployed monthly to staff endpoints and servers. Gap: lab computers at Campus 3 and the campus safety systems are patched irregularly.
EDR runs on all 780 staff endpoints and all cloud servers, monitored 24x7 by the MSSP; lab computers run signature antivirus.
The MSSP monitors SIEM and EDR alerts 24x7. Gaps: no detection for portal account takeover or refund bank changes; no egress alerting on the data warehouse.
The security team receives CISA and vendor advisories and the MSSP's threat bulletins; known exploited vulnerabilities are reviewed weekly.
Gap: no retention and disposal schedule for customer information; financial aid records are kept indefinitely. A schedule that meets 34 CFR 668.24 and 314.4(c)(6) is due 2027-03-31.
Supplier assessments occur at onboarding. Gap: no annual review of Tier 1 vendor SOC 2 reports before this year's first 8 reviews (P09).
